description.narrative: Stakeholder effects Access to Trade Finance for Issuing Banks and Traders. Issuing Banks (IB) in Emerging Markets and Developing Economies (EMDE) face ongoing challenges in the availability of financing to support their customers, who are traders exporting or importing commodities (including critical goods such as food and energy products). These IBs depend on global Confirming Banks (CB) to provide trade financing for their customers. However, due to limitations such as individual counterparty or geographic line limits, increased capital reserve requirements, AML/CFT requirements, and other perceived risks amplified by the recent crises, these CBs are unable to meet the needs of their existing and potential IB counterparts in EMDEs. The GTFP facility will provide trade finance support to DIBPL and its trade finance customers by providing IFC's guarantee through risk mitigation to its counterparty banks, and thereby making these trade-flows happen. These guarantees are especially critical to support trade for lower income and fragile and conflict-affected countries, where the risks are perceived to be higher and likely have very few (if any) global CBs willing to participate.

The Project is an unfunded trade finance facility to Dubai Islamic Bank Pakistan Limited (DIBPL or the Bank) of up to US$ 20 million under IFCs Global Trade Finance Program (GTFP or the GTFP Facility) for transactions with tenors of up to one year. The purpose of the proposed IFC trade line is to support DIBPLs trade program in lieu of challenging macroeconomic conditions in Pakistan.
